description: Deterministic correlation rules. An edge is created from finding A to finding B when A has source_tag, B has target_tag, and the scope condition holds. Scope: same_asset | connected (A's asset connects to B's asset, or same asset).

rules.name: Exposed surface with default credentials
rules.explanation: An internet-reachable admin surface combined with default credentials gives an attacker an authenticated foothold without any exploit.

rules.name: Unthrottled login to weak credentials
rules.explanation: Without rate limiting, credential guessing runs at machine speed, making default or weak passwords a certainty rather than a chance.

rules.name: Information leak accelerates IDOR discovery
rules.explanation: Leaked internal names, schemas or identifiers tell an attacker exactly which object IDs and endpoints to try.

rules.name: Information leak accelerates SSRF targeting
rules.explanation: Leaked internal hostnames and API shapes point the attacker at the internal services an SSRF can reach.

rules.name: Admin foothold reaches data access
rules.explanation: An authenticated administrative foothold on a connected system unlocks functionality that reads or exports data.

rules.name: Admin foothold reaches sensitive store
rules.explanation: The compromised admin surface has a direct network path to a store of sensitive records.

rules.name: IDOR reaches sensitive store
rules.explanation: Object-level authorization failures let the attacker enumerate records from the connected sensitive store.

rules.name: Data access leads to exfiltration
rules.explanation: Broad data access on a system connected to the sensitive store turns a single read into bulk exfiltration.

rules.name: Weak TLS exposes insecure cookies
rules.explanation: Downgradable transport plus cookies without the Secure flag means session tokens can be captured on the wire.

rules.name: Captured session bypasses weak auth
rules.explanation: A captured session cookie is replayed against an identity layer that lacks additional checks such as MFA.

rules.name: SSRF pivots to unauthenticated service
rules.explanation: The SSRF acts as a tunnel from the internet to an internal service that trusts anything on the network.

rules.name: Session store compromise enables data access
rules.explanation: Read/write access to live sessions lets the attacker impersonate any user against the connected API.

rules.name: Forged identity reaches data access
rules.explanation: Unverified tokens let the attacker claim any identity, which the connected API then trusts for sensitive operations.

rules.name: CORS misconfiguration steals tokens
rules.explanation: A malicious site can read authenticated responses, harvesting tokens that the weak token service then accepts.

rules.name: Weak authentication reaches data access
rules.explanation: A weak identity layer in front of a data-access function means one phished or guessed credential yields records.

rules.name: Exposed host reaches sensitive store
rules.explanation: A brute-forceable jump host with a direct database route is a one-hop path to the crown jewels.
